On Wed, Jun 12, 2028 at 08:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com> wrote:
> Looping you all in — Asha sent the shape. Key ask: map to dedicated slab sizing plus a fallback that uses a smaller quantized model for extreme peaks.

Summary (numbers below pulled into the attached workbook and sensitivity tabs):

Inputs from Asha (peak window):
- Peak concurrent sessions: 1,400
- Avg tokens per request: 650
- Avg requests per session during a peak interaction: 1.8 -> aggregate peak requests/sec estimate = (1,400 * 1.8) / 60 ≈ 42 requests/sec
- Tokens/sec at peak = 42 req/sec * 650 tokens ≈ 27,300 tokens/sec

Model throughput assumptions (Redwood-optimized runtime with continuous batching):
- 13B (int8, tuned): ~1,300 tokens/sec per A100-80GB-equivalent GPU (p95 tail fits within 300–360ms with batching and prefix caching)
- 70B (int8 quantized): ~2,500 tokens/sec per GPU but with higher memory and cold-start variability; p95 tends to be ~320–420ms depending on sequence length distribution

Sizing scenarios (reserve + headroom):
1) Expected (preferred): run fine-tuned 13B on Dedicated
   - Required GPUs (raw) = ceil(27,300 / 1,300) = 21 GPUs
   - Add 20% operational headroom for spikes + safe autoscaling buffer → 21 * 1.20 = 25.2 → recommend 26 GPUs reserved
   - Notes: With prefix KV caching for repeated prompts we expect effective tokens/sec to improve by ~10% during a session, so this is conservative.

2) Optimistic (use 70B int8 on dedicated):
   - Required GPUs (raw) = ceil(27,300 / 2,500) = 11 GPUs
   - Add 25% headroom due to higher variability → recommend 14 GPUs reserved
   - Tradeoff: lower GPU count but risk of p95 slipping beyond 350ms on long sequences; needs validation in our perf harness.

3) Conservative fallback (mixed strategy):
   - Reserve 16 GPUs (13B) as committed capacity for normal peaks; configure automatic burst to 30 GPUs via Dedicated burst slots + Hosted fallback to 13B quantized variant for excess traffic.
   - This reduces committed cost while preserving availability.

Other operational recommendations:
- Canary the 70B quantized option with 10% traffic during pilot to validate p95 on real traces before upsizing to 70B as primary.
- Configure request-level routing: route premium users to dedicated slab, default to burst/fallback queue when slab utilization > 75%.
- SLA mapping: with 26 GPUs reserved on 13B we project p95 ~320ms under the 90th-percentile peak test; recommend a p95 SLA of 350ms for the pilot with automatic degraded-mode response (truncated generations) if latency breaches.
- Cost note: 26 A100-equivalent reserved GPUs vs 14 for 70B will materially change monthly commit. I put a quick TCO sketch in the workbook (tab: cost_summaries).

Next steps:
- Ben / Priyom: prepare a short deck that contrasts commit vs hybrid fallback costs + risk table.
- Vanessa: send this recommendation to Asha + procurement, attach workbook and a short explanation of fallback behavior.
- We'll schedule a perf run (using NimbleSky trace) to validate the optimistic 70B numbers; allow 48–72 hours for perf capture and analysis.

I attached the workbook with scenario tabs (conservative/expected/optimistic) and a peaking diagram.
